segments.text: We are going to see how a convex lens focuses light.
First, we draw the convex lens and its principal axis.
Notice the three parallel rays of light entering from the left.
Before they hit the lens, these rays are perfectly parallel to each other and to the axis.
As the parallel rays pass through the convex lens, they refract or bend toward the center.
After leading the lens, the rays are no longer parallel, they converge.
Look closely, all three rays meet at exactly one point on the principal axis.
This point is called the focal point, labeled F.
This focusing happens because the lens is thicker in the middle, bending light more at the edges.
A common mistake is thinking rays stay parallel after the lens, but they must converge to focus.
We verify that all three rays meet at F.
In summary, a convex lens takes parallel light and focuses it to a single focal point on the axis.
This point is called the focal point.
